public_rationale: Stargate announced on January 21, 2025 that it intended to invest $500 billion over four years in U.S. infrastructure for OpenAI [e1]. Anthropic announced a $50 billion U.S. infrastructure investment on November 12, 2025, with sites expected to open throughout 2026 [e2]. These announcements do not establish infrastructure built near $1 trillion by March 10, 2026, or a majority serving OpenAI and Anthropic [e1, e2]. They also do not establish a complete total for committed projects [e1, e2]. MSCI's March 24, 2025 analysis compares stock-market concentration around the dot-com peak and early 2025, without comparing infrastructure and its beneficiaries [e3]. The evidence does not settle whether the claimed combination of market concentration around a few companies and infrastructure mostly serving two companies is unprecedented [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The announcements provide no complete infrastructure inventory with overlapping commitments removed, or industry-wide total for measuring the two companies' share [e1, e2].
Planned investment does not establish completed construction or asset values as of March 10, 2026 [e1, e2].
MSCI's stock-market comparison neither establishes nor excludes a precedent matching the combined market-concentration and infrastructure claim [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The AI bubble is unprecedented: the market has built nearly $1 trillion in infrastructure mostly to serve two companies.

statement.excerpt: There has never been a time when the entire market crystallised around a few specific companies — not even the dot com bubble! — and then built an entire infrastructural layer mostly in service of two of them, with a price tag now leering close to the $1tn mark.

from_speaker: There has never been a time
the entire market crystallised around a few specific companies
not even the dot com bubble
mostly in service of two of them
our_interpretation: The two companies are OpenAI and Anthropic, identified by the surrounding discussion.
The ordinary reading concerns an AI infrastructure buildout concentrated on these companies, not literally every traded security.
Mostly means a majority of the relevant infrastructure, measured consistently by cost or capacity.
The claim concerns the accumulated position as of March 10, 2026. Dated project announcements are relevant records, rather than a single company's latest reporting quarter.
Completed construction, announced capital budgets, and multiyear compute purchases must be tested separately because built and price tag do not identify one accounting measure.
No numerical tolerance is imposed on close to $1 trillion. A result dependent on an invented tolerance would remain unresolved.
criteria.support_condition: A consistently measured, nonduplicated infrastructure inventory near $1 trillion shows a majority serving OpenAI and Anthropic, and a defined historical comparison supports the claimed absence of precedent.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comparable inventory establishes materially different scale or a minority serving those companies, or a documented historical episode satisfies the same combined concentration-and-infrastructure criteria.

evidence.explanation: This is an announced deployment plan, not certification of completed assets. It cannot establish the claimed March 2026 industry-wide total.
The announcement anticipates sites opening during 2026. It cannot be treated as evidence that the entire announced investment was already built by the post date.

evidence.locator: Performance contribution of the top 10 stocks, and technology stocks, to the MSCI USA Index
evidence.explanation: A return-contribution measure shows greater concentration in the dot-com comparison period. This challenges a broad uniqueness claim but does not test the combined infrastructure-and-tenant proposition.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A consistently measured infrastructure inventory as of March 10, 2026, with defined geography and projects, overlaps removed, and OpenAI's and Anthropic's combined share measured. It must separate completed assets, capital commitments and compute purchases. Historical research must test the same combined market-concentration and infrastructure criteria.
